title: H004: Add fsutil test coverage and reference docs
description:
**Size:** 🔧 small
**Category:** testing
**Priority:** medium
**Source:** Proposed for 'Perform a GAP analysis. The README.md as well as'

Create internal/fsutil/atomic_test.go with tests covering atomic file write operations (successful write, permission errors, partial write recovery, concurrent access). Create docs/reference/backend/fsutil.md following the existing pattern of other docs/reference/backend/*.md files, documenting the atomic file operations API, usage examples, and error handling semantics.

**Rationale:** internal/fsutil/atomic.go has zero test coverage — atomic file operations are critical for data integrity (config files, state persistence). A bug here silently corrupts data. Additionally, fsutil is the only internal package without a reference doc page, breaking documentation completeness.

**Affected Areas:**
- internal/fsutil/atomic_test.go
- docs/reference/backend/fsutil.md

requirements.description: WriteFileAtomic SHALL write data atomically to dir/name so that readers never observe a partially-written file
requirements.rationale: Atomic writes are the core guarantee of the function; used for identity, keys, checksums, and cache persistence

scenarios.name: Successful write creates correct file
scenarios.when: WriteFileAtomic is called with a valid directory, name, data, and permissions
scenarios.then: the file at dir/name contains exactly the provided data bytes
and_then: the file has the requested permission mode
no temporary file (.tmp-name) remains

scenarios.name: Write uses temp file and rename
scenarios.when: WriteFileAtomic creates the file
scenarios.then: a temporary file .tmp-name is created first, then renamed to the final name
and_then: the rename is atomic on POSIX systems

scenarios.name: File content is fsynced before rename
scenarios.when: data is written to the temp file
scenarios.then: f.Sync() is called before closing and renaming
and_then: data durability is ensured even on power loss

requirements.description: WriteFileAtomic SHALL return an error and leave no temp file when the directory is not writable
requirements.rationale: Permission errors must propagate cleanly to callers (registration, nodeapi) so they can log and retry

scenarios.name: Read-only directory returns permission error
scenarios.when: WriteFileAtomic is called with a directory that has no write permission
scenarios.then: a non-nil error is returned wrapping the OS permission error
and_then: no target file is created
no temporary file is left behind

scenarios.name: Non-existent directory returns error
scenarios.when: WriteFileAtomic is called with a directory that does not exist
scenarios.then: a non-nil error is returned
and_then: the error wraps the underlying os.ErrNotExist or path error

scenarios.name: Temp file cleanup on open failure
scenarios.when: os.OpenFile fails for the temp file
scenarios.then: no temp file or target file exists after the call returns

requirements.description: WriteFileAtomic SHALL preserve the original file content when a subsequent write fails
requirements.rationale: Critical for data integrity — a failed config update must not corrupt the existing config

scenarios.name: Original file preserved on write failure
scenarios.when: a file already exists at dir/name and a new WriteFileAtomic fails (e.g. disk full simulation)
scenarios.then: the original file content remains unchanged
and_then: the temp file is cleaned up by the deferred os.Remove

scenarios.name: Original file preserved on sync failure
scenarios.when: f.Sync() fails after writing data
scenarios.then: the original file at dir/name is not modified
and_then: the temp file is removed

scenarios.name: Original file preserved on close failure
scenarios.when: f.Close() fails after sync
scenarios.then: the rename does not occur and the original file is intact

requirements.description: WriteFileAtomic SHALL be safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines writing to the same file
requirements.rationale: Multiple subsystems (reconcile, nodeapi cache) may trigger writes concurrently

scenarios.name: Concurrent writes all succeed
scenarios.when: 20 goroutines each call WriteFileAtomic on the same dir/name 50 times
scenarios.then: no goroutine returns an error
and_then: the file exists with valid content after all goroutines complete

scenarios.name: No data race under race detector

scenarios.name: No leftover temp files after concurrent access
scenarios.when: concurrent writes complete
scenarios.then: the directory contains only the target file, no .tmp- files

requirements.description: WriteFileAtomic SHALL handle edge cases: empty data, large payloads, overwriting existing files
requirements.rationale: Boundary conditions must not cause panics or corruption

implementation_notes:
This feature has two deliverables: a test file and a reference doc.

**Test file (internal/fsutil/atomic_test.go):**
- Package: `fsutil` (same package, white-box testing consistent with integrity/store_test.go pattern)
- Use `t.TempDir()` for all temp directories (auto-cleanup)
- Use standard `testing` package only — no external test frameworks per project convention
- Test permission errors by creating a dir then calling `os.Chmod(dir, 0500)` to make it read-only
- Test concurrent access with sync.WaitGroup pattern matching integrity/store_test.go:TestStore_ConcurrentAccess
- Test preservation of original content by: write v1, chmod dir 0500, attempt write v2 (fails), chmod dir back 0700, read file, assert v1 content
- Run with `-race` flag to catch data races

**Reference doc (docs/reference/backend/fsutil.md):**
- Follow the exact front matter pattern: title, quadrant (backend), package (internal/fsutil), feature (PXD-0034)
- Structure: intro paragraph → function signature → parameter table → return value → atomicity guarantee → error handling → usage examples → callers section
- Keep doc concise — fsutil has a single exported function, so this is a small doc
- Reference the 4 calling packages with their specific use cases for context

**Key patterns to follow:**
- integrity/store_test.go: concurrent access test pattern, t.TempDir() usage, error assertion style
- registration/identity_test.go: file permission verification pattern, read-back verification
- docs/reference/backend/integrity-verification.md: front matter format, section structure
- docs/reference/backend/log-forwarding.md: config/API documentation pattern

**Risks:**
- Permission tests may behave differently if running as root (skip with `if os.Getuid() == 0 { t.Skip() }`)
- The concurrent write test uses the same .tmp-name for all goroutines, which is the actual production concern — the test should verify this works despite potential temp file contention
